title: Why modules exist
learningObjectives: Explain why modules exist and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Modules divide a program into files with explicit imports and exports. They provide module scope, help separate responsibilities, and make dependencies visible. Browser ES modules use import and export syntax and are loaded as modules.
understand.whyItMatters: Modules reduce accidental global variables and help teams maintain larger applications. Clear boundaries make testing and refactoring easier.
understand.analogy: A module is a labelled toolbox that exposes only the tools other parts of the program need.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The app module imports a named function from another module. In a browser, use script type=module and serve files over an appropriate origin.

examples.explanation: The app module imports a named function from another module. In a browser, use script type=module and serve files over an appropriate origin.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Split a small script into a data module and a UI module. List the dependency direction and exported public API.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: What is one main purpose of JavaScript modules?
options: To organise code with explicit scope and dependencies
questions.answer: To organise code with explicit scope and dependencies
questions.explanation: Modules provide scope and explicit import/export relationships.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
